newsitem.title: INDIA: India sets rules for private air cargo firms.
newsitem.headline: India sets rules for private air cargo firms.

text.p: Private Indian air cargo operators wanting to fly to foreign destinations will need special permission from the government, the United News of India (UNI) said on Wednesday.
The news agency quoted a spokesman as saying that India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) had issued a set of guidelines for international cargo operations.

The operators would be required to obtain authorisation from the concerned foreign aeronautical authorities before starting operations for which the DGCA might give letters of introduction, the UNI said.
UNI said the operators' services would be outside the purview of the bilateral services agreements.

UNI said private cargo operators with a valid operating permit with plans to operate cargo flights to foreign destinations in accordance with the new guidelines would be required to apply to the office of the DGCA to run flights.
Interested parties would be required to submit details of the proposed operation including the type of aircraft, route, the flight dates and timings, it said.
The DGCA would require atleast 10 days to process any such application, it added.
